defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:768 - `if buf_t.rstrip().endswith("\\"):` tests the raw TEXT, which still carries both characters of an escaped backslash; `_shell_scan` correctly blanks both in the MASK but the join reads text. Measured in bash: a file containing `set -uo pipefail` / `echo \\` / `mkdir -p /proc/nope/child` / `echo reached` run under `bash -e` prints `\`, then `mkdir: cannot create directory '/proc/nope'`, then EXIT=1 with `reached` never printed - two commands, the second fatal. `_logical_lines` on the same body returns `[(1,1,'set -uo pipefail'), (2,3,'echo \\mkdir -p ../scratch'), (4,4,'echo done')]` - ONE command whose first word is `echo`, so `_headed_by(command, "echo")` is True and `_carved_out` admits it. End to end on the real file: inserting `echo \\` + `mkdir -p ../scratch` above `case "$verdict" in` in .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml leaves `bash -n` clean and the WHOLE module at 312 passed - `test_every_command_that_can_fail_sits_in_an_if_or_an_or_list` green, and `test_the_classifier_reads_every_line_of_the_step` green too, because the swallowed line is inside a command rather than blanked. `mkdir -p ../scratch` is this file's own armed-control marker, which the here-string test requires the guard to name in the bare position. The assignment branch swallows the same way: `hk=a\\` + `mkdir -p /proc/nope/child` joins to `hk=a\mkdir -p /proc/nope/child`, matches `_ASSIGNMENT`, carries no `$(`/backtick/redirect, and is carved out. Site predates round 4 (git log -L on that line: 8a19702).

defects.summary: `_classified`'s `case`-pattern heuristic marks an ENTIRE one-line case arm as punctuation - guarded, unread by every rule - whenever the arm's masked text ends in `)` with more `)` than `(`. An assignment whose right-hand side is a `$( )`, or a subshell, placed on the same line as its pattern is silently exempted, defeating the one asymmetry the carve-out list says it exists to enforce.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1945-1946 - `if (mask.rstrip().endswith(")") and mask.count(")") > mask.count("(")): classified.append((start, head, True))`. The rule only counts parens, so an arm body that happens to end in `)` tips the count. Measured against the real body: splicing the arm `zzz) drift=$(mkdir -p /proc/nope/c) ;;` into `case "$verdict" in` classifies as `guarded=True: 'zzz) drift=$(mkdir -p /proc/nope/c)'`; running `case zzz in` / that arm / `esac` / `echo reached` under `bash -e` exits non-zero with `reached` never printed. Same for `zzz) x=$(false) ;;` and `zzz) (mkdir -p /proc/nope/c) ;;` - all three guarded=True, all three abort. The two-line arms the step actually ships (`stale|missing|unreadable)` on its own line, `fresh|unavailable|"$drift")` on its own line) are handled correctly, so nothing today reds - which is why a maintainer collapsing an arm onto one line loses the guard silently. End to end on the real file: appending ` x=$(mkdir -p ../scratch)` to the existing `fresh|unavailable|"$drift")` line in .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml leaves `bash -n` clean and the whole module at 312 passed. This directly overrides the carve-out list's stated rule at scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1846-1850: 'an assignment whose right-hand side is a `$( )` takes that command's status and can abort the step, so it is deliberately NOT carved out.' Site predates round 4 (8a19702).

defects.summary: `_strip_heredocs`' new docstring asserts that EVERY misreading of a heredoc opener 'ends the same way - a delimiter that no later line equals, and a tail blanked to the end of the body', so the new `assert delim is None` covers all of them. The opposite misreading exists, is reachable with no exotic input, and the assertion cannot see it: `line.strip() == delim` ends a heredoc at an INDENTED terminator that bash treats as data.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:711-713 carries the universal claim; scripts/test_account_workflows.py:729 is `if line.strip() == delim:`, which ignores the `-?` the regex captured and ignores column position entirely. Measured in bash: `cat <<EOF` / `line1` / `  EOF` / `line2` / `EOF` / `echo AFTER` prints `line1`, `  EOF`, `line2`, `AFTER` - the indented `EOF` is DATA and the heredoc runs to the column-0 one. `<<-EOF` with a SPACE-indented `  EOF` behaves the same way, because `<<-` strips TABS only. `_strip_heredocs` on that identical body ends the heredoc at `  EOF` and hands back `line2` and the real `EOF` as live shell lines - the tail is UN-blanked, no delimiter is missing, and `assert delim is None` never fires. In the shipped step that misreading is silent rather than loud, which is the direction the docstring promises cannot happen: splicing `    PY` plus a command into the Python heredoc leaves the guard green and the coverage control green, because everything un-blanked is folded into the single logical line `verdict=$(python3 - <<'PY' ... ) || verdict=""`, whose final `||` marks the whole blob guarded - I dumped the segment and it comes back `guarded=True` starting at line 55. Round 4 (ae74589) wrote both the claim and the assertion it justifies.
